 The Tiny Flaw Behind Land Rover's Huge 90,000 Vehicle Recall In October 2026
 By   Ali Hassan 
 Nov. 4, 2026 8:45 am EST 
 Land Rover 
 Add SlashGear on Google: 
 Preferred Source 
 Google Discover 
 If you own a 2022 through 2026 Land Rover Range Rover, it is time to check your VIN . The British automaker recalled 93,997 of these SUVs in the U.S. in October 2026. According to the latest NHTSA recall filing, the affected Range Rovers were built between July 8, 2021, and June 4, 2026. The problem is that there aren't enough drainage holes in the tailgate trim, allowing water to collect around the rearview camera instead of draining away. Over time, that water can damage the camera, leaving drivers with a distorted picture or no image at all when reversing. Land Rover estimates that all 93,997 recalled SUVs have the drainage flaw, regardless of whether their rearview cameras have actually failed.
 It's also not the first time Land Rover has had trouble with water damaging rearview cameras. Similar problems led to recalls involving Range Rover and Range Rover Sport models in January 2024, another batch of Range Rovers in December 2024, and Discovery SUVs as recently as July 2026.
 A failed backup camera can leave pedestrians or obstacles hidden in the SUV's blind spots, with potentially serious consequences. If you've ever wondered why modern cars have so many cameras , this is part of the reason. Backup cameras have been federally required on all new passenger vehicles since May 2018.
 Land Rover found the issue in warranty claims
 Land Rover 
 Land Rover opened an investigation on July 31, 2026, after noticing unusually high rearview camera replacement rates in the U.S. and Canada. It began reviewing warranty claims and sending replaced cameras back to the supplier for inspection. On October 6, the supplier reported that most of the returned cameras it examined had suffered water damage. Land Rover approved the recall two days later.
 Between August 2022 and September 2026, the automaker received 2,295 claims and field reports in the U.S. involving camera replacements. Fortunately, it reported no related crashes, injuries, or fires.
 As for the fix, Land Rover dealers will drill additional drain holes into the underside of the tailgate trim and check whether the camera is working properly. Any camera that needs replacing will be replaced, and owners won't have to pay for the work. Land Rover had already introduced an updated seal on newly built vehicles on June 4, 2026, before the investigation officially began.
 Dealers were scheduled to receive recall notifications on October 29, while owners should receive their initial letters by December 11, 2026. A second notice will follow once the permanent repair is available. To see whether  your car is affected by the recall , you can contact Land Rover at 800-637-6837 or enter your VIN on NHTSA's recall lookup or Land Rover's own recall website .
